newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS-Anglo seen exploring Lonrho options.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Anglo seen exploring Lonrho options.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd could pursue a number of options after backing down in the face of European Union opposition and agreeing to cut its stake in Lonrho Plc to 9.99 percent.
The European Commission, the EU's executive arm, said on Wednesday Anglo had agreed to cut its stake from 27.5 percent but the South African conglomorate said it was "very disappointed".

"However, we have two years in which to divest this stake, a good relationship with Lonrho and a number of options to consider, so we are confident of a satisfactory outcome," Anglo chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson said in a statement.
Analysts said Anglo had only been interested in Lonrho's interest in West African gold producer Ashanti Goldfields Company Ltd and Lonrho Sugar.
"Over the past six months, Anglo has been able to run its eye over the pick of Lonrho's assets," Investec Securities investment analyst John Clemmow said.
Clemmow said as part of its plans, Anglo could sell off the stake agreed with the EU to JCI Ltd or Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd.
"An attractive commercial offer of around the 200 pence level would probably be acceptable from anyone but at prices below this level, one must find companies in which Anglo has an interest".
Lonrho shares are currently trading at 136 pence.
"Putting JCI and Lonrho together makes deal-driven sense and was seriously considered last year," Clemmow said.

But he added that JCI's new control structure, made necessary by strict funding requirements after black empowerment consortium African Mining Group bought JCI earlier this year, would make any potential deal very complex.
"A Lonrho takeover of Gold Fields could make more sense.
Anglo spokeswoman Charmane Russell said the company did not want to disclose details of its various options.
"In terms of looking at our other options, we're obviously not willing to disclose details at this stage.
"But a lot of that is dependent on the fact that we now have sufficient time to work out a constructive solution which is suitable to both Lonrho and ourselves," Russell said.
Anglo said its stake in Lonrho was 25.8 percent while the European Commission considered 1.6 percent of Lonrho held by Anglo-controlled Southern Life as part of its shareholding.

The EU has said Anglo's stake in Lonrho -- which has substantial interests in two South African platinum mines -- would put control of the world's platinum industry in the hands of Anglo American and another South African mining house, Gencor Ltd.
Russell said Anglo's present relationship with Lonrho was very amicable.
"Our relationship is very cordial. We have been very supportive of them, of the way in which they are running the company," she added.
